subject: Dedicated capacity performance validation — SLO/throughput follow-up
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmeai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-10T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Recap + next steps — Dedicated capacity performance validation

Alex — thanks for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on SLOs and validation plan.

Summary of Acme AI SLOs you called out:
- 95th pct latency for streaming responses: <= 200ms
- 99th pct tail for non-streamed completion (up to 512 tokens): <= 350ms
- Sustained throughput target: 250K tokens/min (peak bursts to 400K tokens/min)
- Concurrent active streams: 120
- Support for streaming with partial tokens (server push) and reconnect semantics

Initial sizing questions we agreed to validate:
1) GPU candidate comparison: H100 (80GB), A100 (80GB), and L4 (for cheaper offload) — which meets latency/throughput for your prompt mix
2) Reserved throughput (tokens/sec) per GPU and how many GPUs to reserve for predictable SLOs
3) Impact of KV cache on multi-turn conversations (avg turn length ~60 tokens, 6 turns)
4) Networking: expected egress per minute and whether single-region deployment suffices

Proposed next steps (owner in parentheses):
- You: share 24-48h sample of production traces or a small synthetic workload (we discussed anonymized traces) (Alex)
- Us: run a 2-day dedicated-capacity validation across H100 and A100 shapes using your trace; produce throughput/latency curves by concurrency (Marissa)
- Legal/Procurement touchpoint to align on on-prem/private terms & initial reserved commit (Aditya)
- Quick sync next Fri 6/12 to review results and confirm sizing (all)

Attachments: initial throughput_test_results.pdf (sample kpis) and SLA-draft-acmeai.docx (starter) — see attached.

If that matches your view, please reply with timeline for the traces and any constraints on test dates.

Thanks,
Rafael
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmeai.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acmeai.com>
Date: 2026-06-10T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps — Dedicated capacity performance validation

Thanks Rafael — that summary is great and covers everything we discussed. A few clarifications:
- The 95th pct target is for the user-visible stream, so partial tokens should start arriving within 200ms of first token generation.
- Throughput numbers you quoted are for total token output; we typically have 60/40 ratio of generation vs embedding calls in peak windows.

We will:
- Share a 48h anonymized trace by EOD Monday (6/15).
- Procurement looped in here; we'll need a baseline quote for 3-month reserved capacity and an optional scale-up clause.

Looking forward to the validation results.

—Alex
Head of Platform, Acme AI
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmeai.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-11T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps — Dedicated capacity performance validation

Alex — quick note on the validation plan and what we'll measure so procurement has concrete numbers for the reserved commit: 
- For each GPU class (H100, A100) we'll run three load profiles: steady-state, 2x burst, and high-concurrency ramp.
- We'll report tokens/sec per GPU, p50/p95/p99 latencies for both streaming and non-streaming completions, and memory utilization with KV caching enabled.
- Expected deliverables: benchmarking report (pdf), recommended reserved GPU count for your sustained and burst targets, and a cost projection for a 3-month reserved contract.

If you have any constraints on test windows (e.g., maintenance windows) let us know. We expect runs to take ~6-8 hours per GPU class to collect stable curves; full comparison will be delivered within 48 hours after we receive the traces.

Marissa
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmeai.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-11T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps — Dedicated capacity performance validation

Alex / Procurement — adding procurement/ops checklist so we can expedite reserved capacity: 
- Signed MSA + SOW or a purchase order pointing to DEAL-2026-007
- Initial commit estimate (we'll provide conservative and aggressive sizing after validation)
- Network peering / VPC access window and test IP allowlist
- Data handling requirements for traces (we can accept anonymized offsite uploads to our secure bucket)

I'll start drafting a 3-month reserved quote based on our baseline assumptions and will iterate once Marissa's benchmarks land.

Thanks,
Aditya
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmeai.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acmeai.com>
Date: 2026-06-12T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps — Dedicated capacity performance validation

Rafael / Marissa — we uploaded the anonymized 48h trace to the drive link you provided and gave access to the ops team. Files: acme_trace_20260601-03.tar.gz (anonymized), prompt_profile.csv. Procurement — we'll review your draft SLA and the 3-month commit once Aditya shares it.
